subject: person sitting at desk
title: What If You Sat All Day, Every Day?

scenes.text: What if you sat all day, every day? The damage starts in the first hour.
After one hour of sitting, the arteries in your legs can work up to 50 percent worse.
Your big leg muscles go almost silent, so they stop helping pump blood back to your heart.
Sit for four hours or more, like on a long flight, and the risk of a blood clot in your legs roughly doubles.
Over years, eight hours a day of sitting with little exercise is linked to a much higher risk of dying early.
The fix is small: short walks protected the arteries, and an hour of brisk walking a day erased the extra risk.

description:
What if you sat all day, every day? In an Indiana University study, one hour of sitting cut leg-artery function by up to 50 percent, and three 5-minute walks prevented it. WHO's travel study found the risk of blood clots roughly doubles after 4 or more hours of sitting travel.
A 2016 Lancet analysis of over a million people found 60 to 75 minutes of moderate activity a day removed the extra early-death risk linked to sitting 8 hours a day (an association).
